To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) presynaptic Ca2+ currents are responsible for evoking quantal release at the neuromuscular synapse and (2) the time delay from the onset of a presynaptic action potential to the appearance of the first postsyntaptic quantal event is variable and can be as great as 100 msec.

the presynaptic Ca current that underlies synaptic transmission in the avian neuromucular junction is a single type of channel with slow kinetics, that synaptic delay is long for weak stimuli, but short for stronger stimuli, that the time course of the presynaptic current and synaptic delay is well described by the time course of presynaptic calcium currents, and that the time course and amplitude of the presynaptiic Ca current is well fit by a model of calcium channel kinetics that assumes
the presynaptic Ca current is a major determinant of the number and temporal pattern of synaptic transmission at the avian ciliary neuromuscular synapse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between presynaptic Ca+ currents and quantal release from cultured avian ciliary neurons.
the relationship between Ca++ current and quantal release in avian ciliary neurons.
the mechanisms by which presynaptic Ca+ currents are translated into quantal transmission at the neuromuscular synapse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca++ current is the primary trigger for the release of quanta of neurotransmitter.
presynaptic calcium currents are evoked from avian ciliar ganglion neurons.
the presynaptic Ca2+ current is the only factor determining quantal release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presynaptic Ca2+ current and synaptic transmission in avian ciliary neurons are both characterized by a single type of Ca2+ channel with a slow inactivation time constant.

the Ca++ currents responsible for evoked quantal release in the chick neuromuscular system display a slow inactivation and are capable of generating a large number of quantal events in the absence of a significant delay.
the time course of Ca++ entry and the kinetics of the presynaptic calcium current determine the time course of quantal transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca++ current inactivation time constants are not a good predictor of quantal delay.
presynaptic Ca+ currents can be recorded in avian neuromuclar junctions in culture and that they are well correlated with quantal transmission.
the time course of presynaptic calcium currents is a key determinant of the temporal pattern of quantal release at the neuromuscular synapse.
